# vaultwarden_organization_user (Resource)

This resource invites a user to an organization on the Vaultwarden server.

## Example Usage

```terraform
resource "vaultwarden_organization" "example" {
  name = "Example"
}

resource "vaultwarden_organization_user" "example" {
  organization_id = vaultwarden_organization.example.id
  email           = "foo@example.com"
  type            = "User"
}
```

<!-- schema generated by tfplugindocs -->
## Schema

### Required

- `email` (String) The email of the user to invite. Changing it removes the user from the organization and invites the new email.
- `organization_id` (String) ID of the organization to invite the user to

### Optional

- `access_all` (Boolean) Whether the user has access to all collections in the organization. `Owner` and `Admin` users always have access to all collections. For `Manager` users it can be set to `true` (the *Manage all collections* permission). `User` users cannot have it; grant them access to individual collections instead. Defaults to `true` for `Owner` and `Admin`, and `false` otherwise.
- `type` (String) The role type of the user (Owner, Admin, User, Manager). Defaults to `User`

### Read-Only

- `id` (String) ID of the invited user
- `status` (String) The status of the user

## Import

Import is supported using the following syntax:

The [`terraform import` command](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/cli/commands/import) can be used, for example:

```shell
terraform import vaultwarden_organization_user.example <id>
```
